designFidelity: matches — the plan's chosen look is `studio` and `src/index.css` carries the provenance line `Written by scripts/apply-look.js from looks/studio.css` with the studio token set in both themes; the shell and pages are the phone-first single-column form factor the plan asked for (one thing per screen, full-width tap targets, no side-by-side panes).
summary:
Scope of this review is safety and conventions on the code this build wrote, not whether the features work. On that axis the diff is clean: every resource applies the owner rule from api-plan.json (MenuApi/StoreInfoApi/CheckoutApi public, OrderConfirmationApi capability-by-code with no listing, MenuAdminApi/StoreSettingsApi/OrderAdminApi admin on every method including OrderAdminApi.connect, which calls requireAdmin before db.Order.subscribe); refusals are thrown 403 Responses with auth_required/admin_required and no 401 anywhere (the deploy smoke table expects 403 on the three admin roots); no key material is committed and the only new dependency, google-auth-library, is on the template allowlist; the only outbound hosts are api.stripe.com and api.resend.com, both in integrations; no instruction-shaped text in seed data or UI copy; data/ holds preview-only rows with invented customers and nothing was put in data/production/; `run_check lint` is green, rule 18 holds (only lib/db.js names tables/databases), routes/spa.js imports nothing, and every filtered or sorted attribute (available, queue, code, paymentRef, placedAt, loop) is @indexed.

Noted and left to the owner: QA reports POST /MenuAdminApi/update and POST /OrderAdminApi/status answering 400 on the live deployment with the cause unestablished. That is a functional defect, not a hole or a convention breach, and the build has recorded it honestly in CLAUDE.md §7 as an open question with the evidence still needed rather than guessing a third fix — which is the right handling. It is reported by QA and is not mine to hold the publish on.

findings.message: POST /CheckoutApi/order is not idempotent under retry: each call mints a fresh crypto.randomUUID() id and a fresh newOrderCode(), so a double submit or a client retry writes a second Order row. With a Stripe key the duplicate sits in pending_payment and is harmless (the idempotencyKey is the new code, so it does not dedupe either), but with no key configured both rows land status:'received', queue:'active', pay_at_store — two live orders in the kitchen queue for one basket. src/pages/Checkout.tsx does guard with its `submitting` flag, so the exposure is a network retry or a resubmitted request rather than an ordinary double tap, which is why this is minor rather than a blocker. A client-supplied request key (or a deterministic key over the cart plus customer plus minute) carried into a create-on-first-write would close it.

Recorded, not charged against this stage: the update/delete action routes here and POST /OrderAdminApi/status are known to answer 400 on the deployment (QA, two orders and a no-op menu save), and the header comments plus CLAUDE.md §7 correctly state that the theory the shape was changed for has been falsified and the cause is unknown. The code itself breaks no convention I can see — post(target, data), segmentsOf(target), admin re-read on every method — and the probes drive both the action routes and the PUT/PATCH aliases in-process, so nothing hermetic can see this. Flagged only so the next session does not reshape the request a third time before capturing one raw failing response, its headers and body, the server log line beside it and the Harper version, as §7 asks.
